main_body: Two stacked horizontal logs seen from the side, with pale round end-grain faces on the left and long dark bark sides running right
top_band: none. The upper log has a 1-2 row lighter brown stripe along its back edge (rows 3-4), but it is a bark highlight on a cylinder, not a horizontal surface seen from above
evidence: Reading down a column through the middle of the bark body, there is a thin light edge stripe at rows 3-4, then dark brown bark down to the log's lower edge. This is a log profile, and the circular end faces on the left are vertical faces, not tops. No horizontal surface is visible from above, there is no distinct front-edge line, and no eave shadow. The piece reads as a side elevation of a log stack, so it fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The end grain has a decent cream ramp with ring dots, and the outline is a dark brown tinted to the wood. The bark sides, however, are large near-flat dark brown areas with only a few highlight pixels and no grain or knots. The tiles carry fewer colours than the stall and well references, so the piece looks thinner and flatter beside them.
